title: survey
description: A dossier: what is already true in this repository, for a task that has not been planned yet. Every claim here is mechanically re-checkable against the tree, which is the only reason it is safe to let a local model produce it.

understanding.description: What the task is asking for, in your own words, in terms of the behaviour a user would notice. Do not propose a design here.

searches.description: Every search you ran that informed this dossier. These are REPLAYED against a clean checkout and the file list compared against what you claim, so record the command exactly as you ran it.

command.description: The literal shell command, runnable from the repository root.

why.description: What you were trying to find out.

result_paths.description: The distinct file paths the command returned. If there were more than 20, list the first 20 and set truncated true.

evidence.description: The specific code that matters, quoted. Each quote is checked byte-for-byte against the file you name: a quote that is not there is a fabrication and voids the dossier. Copy, never retype.

quote.description: Copied verbatim from the file, including its indentation.

what_it_shows.description: Why a planner needs to know this. Not a restatement of the quote.

change_surface.description: Every file that would have to be created or modified. This is the most important list in the dossier: the plan that follows may only touch files named here, so a file you miss is a file the implementation cannot use.

exists.description: true if the file is already in the tree, false if it would be created.

change.description: What would change in it, in one or two sentences.

why.description: What makes this file necessary rather than incidental.

conventions.description: How this codebase does things of the kind the task needs. Every convention must carry an example quoted from a real file, for the same reason evidence must: an unevidenced convention is a guess wearing authority.

existing_tests.description: Tests that already cover the area, and would therefore either have to keep passing or be extended.

verification_commands.description: Commands that would prove the task is done. Each must FAIL on the tree as it stands today — a command that already passes proves nothing — and each must be a real command, not a description of one.

unknowns.description: What you could not determine, stated plainly. This field is not a failure: an honest unknown costs one question, and a confident guess costs a wrong plan. Leave it empty only if it is genuinely empty.
